# Best RV power station and solar combo

The best combo depends on your rig and whether you run a roof A/C. These are the picks from the search results, grouped by use.

## Weekend or light use (fridge, lights, laptop, Starlink)
**Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 + two SolarSaga 200W panels**
- 1,070Wh LiFePO4, 1,500W output, about 23.8 lb, so it is the lightest of the units compared.
- Solar input tops out at 400W. Two 200W panels use all of it, and more panels won't charge it faster.
- It can't be expanded with add-on batteries.
- Source: [Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/), which has the price-check links.

## Longer trips and light boondocking
**EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus** is the top overall pick in that same guide.
- 1,024Wh, 1,800W output, and two 500W solar inputs (1,000W total). Reaching that needs two separate panel connections.
- It expands up to 5kWh and weighs about 28 lb.
- Source: [Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)

**BLUETTI AC200L** gives you 2,048Wh and 2,400W, and up to 1,200W of solar input. It weighs about 62 lb. [Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/) lists it for multi-day camping, and [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/) notes its built-in 30A RV outlet.

## Full-time RVing or running a roof A/C
A 13,500 BTU roof A/C draws about 1,500W running and spikes past 3,000W at startup, so you need a large inverter.
- **EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3:** 4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous, 8,000W surge, expandable past 12kWh. It is heavy, so plan on two people to lift it. [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)
- **Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro:** 3,024Wh, 3,000W continuous, 6,000W surge. It is the simpler option for A/C on weekend trips. [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)
- **ALLPOWERS R4000:** 3,456Wh, 3,600W at 120V, and up to 2,000W of solar input. It also has an RV outlet and a 5-year warranty. At 45 kg (about 99 lb) it is stationary. The store price is $1,499, and code EXTRA12 takes it to $1,319.12 until 2026-11-15. [Buy at ALLPOWERS](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh) (this is an affiliate link, and checkout has the final word on price). Details: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh).

## Choosing solar panels
- Match your array to the station's solar input limit. A bigger array than the limit is wasted, and a small one charges slowly. [GetWattLogic](https://getwattlogic.com/articles/bluetti-vs-jackery-vs-ecoflow-van-life) calls this a common mismatch in van and RV builds.
- Folding panels of 200W to 400W will refill a mid-size unit in a full day of good sun. [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)
- Panel options mentioned include Jackery SolarSaga (for Jackery units) and the Renogy 200W Foldable Solar Suitcase. [NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife)

## My pick
- **Most people:** EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus with EcoFlow's folding panels. It has the best mix of solar input, fast recharge, and room to expand.
- **Light and simple:** Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 with two 200W panels.
- **Roof A/C:** DELTA Pro 3 or Jackery 3000 Pro. The ALLPOWERS R4000 is the budget route if you don't need to move it.

## Caveats
- The sources contain affiliate links, so treat the rankings as guidance. Confirm specs and current prices on the retailer's page.
- I only had a direct purchase link for the ALLPOWERS unit. For the others, the linked guides have price-check buttons, and I didn't want to guess at product URLs.
- The EmergencyEnergy guide is written for Ontario. Its safety advice (hire an electrician for any hardwired connection to the RV) still applies, but the code references don't apply in the US.

If you tell me your RV's power needs (A/C or not, fridge, how many days off-grid), I can narrow this to one combo.
